newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HINGIS, SANCHEZ VICARIO ADVANCE AS INJURIES MOUNT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS, SANCHEZ VICARIO ADVANCE AS INJURIES MOUNT.

text.p: Swiss tennis starlet Martina Hingis and Spain's world number two Arantxa Sanchez Vicario swept into the third round of the Australian Open on Thursday as around them the tournament's injury toll climbed higher.

Germany's Anke Huber, whose mother added her name to the casualty list when she mysteriously collapsed here on Wednesday, also won through, although Italy's Francesca Lubiani gave the world number seven a fright by taking the first set 6-4.

Hingis, a multi-millionaire at the tender age of 16, took just one hour on centre court to dispatch American Lisa Raymond, who offered resistance in the early stages but succumbed to the fourth seed's all-round mastery of the court.
Playing what she said was "almost perfect tennis" in the second set, Hingis finished Raymond off with a crisp forehand volley to break the American's serve and win 6-4 6-2.
She next meets either Barbara Schett of Austria or Alexandra Fusai of France in her bid to become the youngest player to ever win a grand slam event.
Czechoslovak-born Hingis has been in the headlines this week for a five-year deal with an Italian sportswear label worth up to US$12 million if she reaches world number one.
But Hingis complained after her win that too much had been made of the deal and she might only get US$1.4 million a year.
"I would really like to be as rich as they make out in the newspapers. That would be great," Hingis told reporters.
"I don't get all this money. That's the problem."

Sanchez Vicario, whose own path to the Open final has been eclipsed by the hype surrounding Hingis and top seed Steffi Graf, made an unremarkable entry into the third round when her Belgian opponent retired hurt in the second game.
Sanchez Vicario had won the first game when Stephanie de Ville twisted an ankle only three minutes into the match.

De Ville was pushed from the court in a wheelchair, recalling the end to tournament favourite Graf's first round match on Monday when the 21-times grand slam champion ran to Slovakian Janette Husarova's aid shen she twisted a knee.
World number two Monica Seles withdrew from the Open last week, suffering a broken finger.

Huber told reporters on Thursday that her mother, Gerda, had been given a clean bill of health after ambulance officers whisked her to hospital on Wednesday after she collapsed outside the players' lounge.
"She's doing fine and she's coming back this afternoon from hospital and everything was okay," said Huber, whose second-round match was postponed because of the incident.
Asked what caused the collapse, Huber said: "We don't know yet."
In other matches on Thursday, Australian Mark Woodforde showed the same form that took him to a career-best semifinal berth at last year's Open, beating Hernan Gumy of Argentina 6-0 6-1 7-5.
